Latheport 2.0 is in the works.

First up: a video player built from scratch. Early numbers on 4K HEVC, against VLC 3.0.24, same PC:

1.8x faster to open
10.6x faster to jump to a frame
3.3x less processor
4.9x less memory

More to show when it's ready. https://github.com/puretechteam/Latheport

What's in this app? now counts lines of code.

Drop a project's folder on https://puretechteam.github.io/: lines per language, how much is bundled libraries, even the code packed inside Electron apps.

Our own website: 6,210 lines.

Nothing is uploaded.

Farther. A free browser game about charting an unknown world outward from a single campfire.

The first edition is still being drawn.

New on our site: What's in this app?

Drag any program's folder onto the page and see how much of it is the program and how much is extra.

Unity Hub on our PC: 520 MB. 56% is a bundled web browser. 14% is the program itself.

Nothing is uploaded. https://puretechteam.github.io/

Embedding X posts still feels clunky: paste their generated code into your site and let X render it.

The old free API tier is gone for most developers; reads now cost $0.005 per post ($50/10,000).

One-time credits aren't a real free tier.

Game development is a weird process. You can spend hours getting something to work, finally get it running, and then realize it's just not fun.

Sometimes the hardest part isn't building the game. It's figuring out what makes it worth playing.

ChildLock 0.3 got a makeover.

A new Settings window, a tray icon you can actually read, and a badge that fades in instead of popping up.

Same job as before: one shortcut locks your keyboard and mouse while the video keeps playing.

Free for Windows: https://github.com/puretechteam/childlock

Software. Libraries. And now ??

We have started making games. That is all we are saying today.

Latheport 1.5, the new name for ConvertAll: free, open source, for Windows.

New: a photo editor, a video timeline, PDF join, split and compress, and smart tools that run on your PC.

No Ghostscript needed: 1.8x faster PostScript to PDF. https://github.com/puretechteam/Latheport
